question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the Indian Constitution as a Fundamental Duty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**To respect elders**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A citizen of India has no inherent obligation to **amass property.**
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, following traffic laws is not a Basic Responsibility.
 
• **Article 51A of Part IV-A **of the Indian Constitution lists the fundamental obligations of Indian citizens.
 
 
• Respect the national flag, national anthem, and Indian Constitution as well as all of its ideas and institutions.
 
• To uphold and adhere to the lofty values that sparked the country's fight for freedom.
 
• To safeguard and defend India's **sovereignty, unification, and integrity.​**​
 
 
 
• The** moral responsibility** of all people to support the unity of India and advance patriotism are known as the **Basic Obligations**.
 
• These obligations, which are outlined in Section IV-A of the Constitution, affect both people and the country.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​10 Basic Responsibilities were introduced to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.
 
• Later, the 11th Basic Responsibility was included in the list by the 86th Amendment Act of 2002.
 
• In 1976, the **Swaran Singh Committee** proposed Basic Responsibilities.​
 
• The Swaran Singh Committee also advocated for the obligation to pay taxes. Yet, the Constitution did not include it.
 
• The** Constitution's Article 51A **lists the essential obligations.
 
• The **Basic Rights**, **Directive Principles of State Policy**, and** Fundamental Duties **are portions of the Indian Constitution that outline the fundamental duties and **rights of citizens** towards the state as well as the fundamental obligations of states to their inhabitants. 
 
• These articles are regarded as essential parts of the constitution, which was created during 1949 by the **Indian Constituent Assembly**.

4b:T19
